source.section: PDF page 7 'Examples of Income You DO NOT Report' (Defined Benefit Retirement Plan, IRC 414(j); no other-state system named); PDF page 14 Schedule RS list; Form 40 (25f40blk.pdf page 1) lines 5b to 18; booklet PDF page 8 lines 5 to 13, PDF page 10 lines 14 and 17; PDF page 9 Standard Deduction chart (line 11, PDF page 8); Form 40 page 1 boxes 1 to 4 (personal exemption, line 13); tax table PDF pages 25 to 30

worked: Federal AGI = New York State and Local Retirement System pension 36,000.00 + IRA distribution (person 0) 20,000.00 + interest 750.00 = 56,750.00. Federal taxable income = 56,750.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 39,000.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Alabama: the projection starts from federal AGI and removes exempt income (Form 40 builds its own lines 5b to 10, which give the same AGI for this household). Subtract New York State and Local Retirement System pension 36,000.00: no line names New York or another state's system; the IRC 414(j) defined benefit line (PDF page 7; PDF page 14) names a kind of plan with no Alabama limit, so a qualifying New York State pension is not reported; the projection treats every other state's government pension as qualifying (approximation). IRA distribution 20,000.00 and interest 750.00 stay in: taxable (Schedule RS, PDF page 14; Form 40 line 6). Form 40 line 10 Alabama AGI = 20,750.00. Line 11 standard deduction (single, chart PDF page 9): AL AGI 20,750.00 is in the first band (0 to 25,999.00), the full amount, so 3,000.00. Line 12 federal income tax deduction: the form subtracts the 2025 federal income tax (worksheet PDF page 31); the projection does not model it (not_modelled, approximation), so 0.00 here. Line 13 personal exemption (single) 1,500.00. Line 14 dependent exemption 0.00 (no dependents). Line 15 total deductions = 3,000.00 + 0.00 + 1,500.00 + 0.00 = 4,500.00. Line 16 taxable income = 20,750.00 - 4,500.00 = 16,250.00. Line 17 tax from the derived single / married filing separately / head of family schedule (2% from 0, 4% from 500, 5% from 3,000): (500.00 - 0.00) x 0.02 = 10.00 + (3,000.00 - 500.00) x 0.04 = 100.00 + (16,250.00 - 3,000.00) x 0.05 = 662.50 = 772.50; the tax table row 16,200-16,300 (single / married filing separately / head of family column, PDF pages 25 to 30) gives 773. Line 18 net tax due, no credits: 772.50.
accepted_approximations: The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).

The brackets are derived from the tax table. Under 100,000 the table taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint, rounded; above 100,000 the printed worksheet ((income - 100,000) x .05 + 4,958, or + 4,918 joint) is 2 dollars below the derived brackets.

Every private pension and every other state's government pension is treated as paid by a plan that qualifies as a defined benefit plan under IRC 414(j), and every Alabama or federal government pension as exempt; the booklet exempts only the listed systems and qualifying 414(j) plans and leaves qualification to the plan administrator.
